findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that `exception_type` is in `_ALLOWED_FIELDS`, place it after the `**diagnostic` spread, and assert `coverage.diagnostic["exception_type"] == "LLMBudgetExhaustedError"` in the budget test.
evidence: "it keeps only `_ALLOWED_FIELDS`, which already include the run-shape counters ... (`requests`, `tool_calls`, `request_limit`, `tool_calls_limit`, `finish_reason`)" — exception_type is not listed
Test assertion: "`coverage.diagnostic` has `requests == 41` and `tool_calls == 80` and no `input_tokens`" — no exception_type assertion
Current behaviour per Context: diagnostic is "only `{"exception_type": ...}`"
findings.finding: The plan routes the merged diagnostic through `sanitize_diagnostic`, which 'keeps only `_ALLOWED_FIELDS`'. It lists the run-shape counters as allowed but never states that `exception_type` is in `_ALLOWED_FIELDS`. If it is not, the change silently drops the only field the diagnostic carries today. The new budget test asserts `requests`, `tool_calls` and the absence of `input_tokens`, but not that `exception_type` survives. In addition, `{"exception_type": ..., **diagnostic}` lets a diagnostic key named `exception_type` override the real type.
findings.location: Approach — `_agentic_outcome` `fixed(...)` bullet; Add tests — LLMBudgetExhaustedError case
scenarios: exception_type is not allowlisted, so failed agentic verdicts lose the exception type: a regression no test catches
An exception's diagnostic dict carries an `exception_type` key that overwrites the true class name
findings.suggested_fix: Build the dict as `{**dict(getattr(exc, "diagnostic", {}) or {}), "exception_type": type(exc).__name__}` before sanitizing, and add `assert diag["exception_type"] == "LLMBudgetExhaustedError"` to the budget test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Either add `check_stop_reason("length")`/`("max_tokens")` cases asserting the raised error's `stop_reason`, or state explicitly that truncation is raised elsewhere and why refusal alone closes item 3.
evidence: Context 3: "No test checks that production `structured.check_stop_reason` sets `UnretryableOutputError.stop_reason`; the failure-class tests set it by hand."
Approach tests only `check_stop_reason("refusal")` and a `"refusal"` provider_details key
findings.finding: Context item 3 says the failure-class tests set `stop_reason` by hand. Those are the truncation tests (`max_tokens`, and the new `length` case). Yet the new production-path tests only exercise `check_stop_reason("refusal")` and a refusal `provider_details`. Nothing proves that production sets `stop_reason` to `max_tokens`/`length` for the truncation path that the classification table depends on. The new `length` → CHANGE_SETTINGS test will presumably also hand-set `stop_reason`.
findings.location: Add tests — tests/unit/test_structured.py bullet; `length` truncation bullet
scenarios: Production truncation raises with `stop_reason=None` or a different value, so the CHANGE_SETTINGS classification never fires in real runs while the hand-set table tests pass

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm `exception_type` is in `_ALLOWED_FIELDS`, assert in the budget-exhausted test that `coverage.diagnostic["exception_type"] == "LLMBudgetExhaustedError"`, and put `exception_type` after the spread so it cannot be overridden.
evidence: "build the diagnostic as failure.sanitize_diagnostic({"exception_type": type(exc).__name__, **dict(getattr(exc, "diagnostic", {}) or {})})"
"it keeps only `_ALLOWED_FIELDS`, which already include the run-shape counters ... (`requests`, `tool_calls`, `request_limit`, `tool_calls_limit`, `finish_reason`)" — `exception_type` is not listed
Test asserts "`requests == 41` and `tool_calls == 80` and no `input_tokens`" only
findings.finding: Wrapping the diagnostic in `failure.sanitize_diagnostic` could silently drop `exception_type`, the only key the current diagnostic carries, if that key is not in `_ALLOWED_FIELDS`. The plan names only the run-shape counters as allowlisted. The new budget test asserts `requests`, `tool_calls` and the absence of `input_tokens`, but never that `exception_type` is still present.
scenarios: `exception_type` is not allowlisted, so budget, tool-loop and truncation verdicts lose the exception type while the new tests stay green.
A run-shape diagnostic that itself carries an `exception_type` key overrides the real type because the spread comes after it.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the budget test assertion to `coverage.diagnostic["exception_type"] == "LLMBudgetExhaustedError"`. Order the dict as `{**run_shape, "exception_type": type(exc).__name__}` so the real type always wins.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the DET-advisory/provider_provenance test drives the review through the `gates/plan-review.yaml` workflow (the production entry point), not the adapter directly.
evidence: Context: "No test checks that a DET advisory finding and the agent call's `provider_provenance` reach the adapted agentic verdict through `gates/plan-review.yaml`."
Approach: "reviewed under `engine="agentic"` carries that DET advisory in `advisory`, and the verdict's `provider_provenance` equals what the fake runner stamped" — no mention of the gate YAML
findings.finding: Review finding 4 asks for proof that the DET advisory and `provider_provenance` reach the adapted verdict through `gates/plan-review.yaml`. The planned test only says the plan is reviewed under `engine="agentic"` with a fake runner; it does not say the test runs through the gate YAML. It may therefore exercise the adapter directly and leave the stated gap open.
findings.location: Context item 4 vs Approach — test_plan_review_agentic_verdict.py first bullet
scenarios: The test calls the adapter with a hand-built input, passes, and a broken YAML wiring of the advisory or provenance still ships undetected.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the budget-diagnostic test, set the attribute after construction (`exc = errors.LLMBudgetExhaustedError("budget"); exc.diagnostic = {...}`), as run_failure.py:82 does, instead of passing a `diagnostic=` kwarg the class does not accept.
evidence: Plan: "an `LLMBudgetExhaustedError` carrying `diagnostic={"requests": 41, "tool_calls": 80, "input_tokens": 9}`"
src/rebar/llm/errors.py:143-150: `class LLMBudgetExhaustedError(LLMRunnerError):` declares only a docstring, with no __init__ or diagnostic kwarg
src/rebar/llm/errors.py:191: RunawayToolLoopError.__init__(self, message, *, diagnostic=None) — the sibling that does take the kwarg
src/rebar/llm/run_failure.py:82: production attaches it as `budget_err.diagnostic = budget_diag` (attribute, not a constructor kwarg)
findings.finding: The budget-diagnostic test says to build an `LLMBudgetExhaustedError` "carrying `diagnostic={...}`". That class has no `__init__` taking a `diagnostic` keyword; only `RunawayToolLoopError` and `CompletionRecoveryError` have one. Calling `LLMBudgetExhaustedError("budget", diagnostic={...})` raises TypeError, so the fixture has to set `.diagnostic` as an attribute after construction.
scenarios: The implementer writes `errors.LLMBudgetExhaustedError("budget", diagnostic={...})` by analogy with RunawayToolLoopError, and the test errors with TypeError before it checks anything.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the test bullet to: "an `LLMBudgetExhaustedError` whose `.diagnostic` attribute is set (as `run_failure.interpret_failure` does) to `{"requests": 41, "tool_calls": 80, "input_tokens": 9}`".
